extracted.intended_audience: educators, policymakers, donors, students, and the general public interested in K–12 civic education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and organizational standards for creating, delivering, and evaluating K–12 civic education that prepares students for informed civic participation. Emphasizes curriculum resources, nonpartisanship, engagement methods, policy advocacy, and evidence-based impact measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant, meaningful, and engaging civic education
rubrics_metrics.description: We need civic education that is relevant, meaningful, and engaging for each new generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic education should be tailored to contemporary students so it resonates with them and encourages participation; the phrasing implies prioritizing content and methods that connect to learners' lives and motivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build knowledge, skills, and dispositions for informed civic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: We empower educators with resources that build the knowledge, skills, and dispositions students need for informed civic participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources should not only convey factual knowledge but explicitly develop civic skills (e.g., deliberation, voting literacy) and dispositions (e.g., respect for democratic processes). Materials and professional supports should be oriented toward these three domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free and accessible educational resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking for our free educational resources? Discover free educational resources. Play & Learn. Teach with iCivics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources should be freely available to teachers and students (iCivics states up to 145,000 teachers and 9 million students use its free resources). Accessibility and no-cost distribution are core delivery criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisan materials and fidelity to sustaining democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: iCivics allows me the opportunity and materials to live in a nonpartisan place. ... They really focus on the things that I, and we, want fidelity to: sustaining our democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials and programs should avoid partisan advocacy and instead focus on objective civic knowledge and practices that sustain democratic institutions; fidelity implies consistent adherence to nonpartisan presentation across offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media literacy and source-evaluation skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Students need to know how to find a reliable resource, and how to sift through fake news and AI-generated content to find what is true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic curricula should include explicit instruction and practice in evaluating information sources, detecting misinformation (including AI-generated content), and finding reliable resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage diverse learners and leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: We invite and engage a diverse network of learners and leaders in the movement for high-quality civic education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should proactively reach and include diverse audiences (demographic, geographic, experiential) and involve leaders/stakeholders from varied backgrounds in design and delivery to broaden participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active, participatory strategies (e.g., competitions, projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: “We Declare!” Challenge Launches to Engage Mass 8th Graders in Civics ... 8th grade students across the Commonwealth are invited to bring the Declaration of Independence to life through a statewide video competition ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ experiential, project-based, and competitive formats (video challenges, projects) to increase engagement and practical understanding of civic texts and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy advocacy to prioritize civic education
rubrics_metrics.description: We advance policy at the state and national levels to make civic education a priority for the health and strength of our nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of organizational strategy is to influence policy so that civic education is resourced and prioritized; evaluation of programs may include policy-change activities and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and share evidence-based impact
rubrics_metrics.description: We evaluate and share evidence-based findings that demonstrate the value and impact of civic education for our country’s future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should include rigorous evaluation (data collection, analysis) and public dissemination of results to demonstrate effectiveness and justify support; 'evidence-based' implies use of accepted research methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and high-quality civic education as an outcome metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who receive a comprehensive and high-quality civic education, are more likely to be informed and actively engaged citizens and voters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program success should be judged by whether instruction is comprehensive (covers necessary content/skills) and high-quality (effective pedagogy), with downstream outcomes such as informed engagement and voting behavior used as indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrate impact through stories and concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact Stories — Illustrating the impact we make ... Read more from Satu (Student/Youth Fellow), Kristy (Adult Education Instructor), Shari (AP teacher).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative impact narratives (student/teacher testimonials, case studies) alongside quantitative evaluation to illustrate program effects and to communicate value to stakeholders and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and reach as a measure of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Today, up to 145,000 teachers and 9 million students in all 50 states utilize iCivics’ innovative and free resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breadth of adoption (number of teachers/students, geographic coverage across states) is presented as an indicator of program reach and success; scaling access is an operational metric.
